text: Identify the report as a systematic review.
note: Titled as a systematic literature audit of the CLAD literature; the design is a meta-research reporting audit, not a review of intervention effects.

text: See the PRISMA 2020 for Abstracts checklist.
note: Structured abstract.

text: Describe the rationale for the review in the context of existing knowledge.
Provide an explicit statement of the objective(s) or question(s) the review addresses.
note: Three questions stated explicitly.

text: Specify the inclusion and exclusion criteria for the review and how studies were grouped for the syntheses.
note: Eligibility keys on study structure. Confirmed exclusions are recorded per identifier with a reason and available with the study data.

text: Specify all databases, registers, websites, organisations, reference lists and other sources searched or consulted to identify studies. Specify the date when each source was last searched or consulted.
location: Methods, Design and search; Supplement S1
note: Single source (PubMed via E-utilities); query frozen 5 August 2026.

text: Present the full search strategies for all databases, registers and websites, including any filters and limits used.
note: Query reproduced verbatim from the pipeline source at render time.

text: Specify the methods used to decide whether a study met the inclusion criteria of the review, including how many reviewers screened each record and each report retrieved, whether they worked independently, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.
location: Methods, Eligibility and Extraction; Supplement S2, S3, S7
note: Screening was automated: a title/abstract classifier over all screened records, then a full-text pass. No dual human screening. Both automated steps were validated against a blinded expert reference standard (S7).

text: Specify the methods used to collect data from reports, including how many reviewers collected data from each report, whether they worked independently, any processes for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.
location: Methods, Extraction; Supplement S3, S4, S7
note: Single-pass language-model extraction under an evidence-grounded protocol; prompts verbatim in S4. No contact with study investigators. Validated against an expert reference standard on a blinded subset.

text: List and define all outcomes for which data were sought. Specify whether all results that were compatible with each outcome domain in each study were sought (e.g. for all measures, time points, analyses), and if not, the methods used to decide which results to collect.
location: Methods, Covariate panel and Analysis; Supplement S6
note: The outcome is reporting completeness per covariate, scored 0/1/2 against pre-specified anchors (S6).

text: List and define all other variables for which data were sought (e.g. participant and intervention characteristics, funding sources). Describe any assumptions made about any missing or unclear information.
note: Study-level covariates listed in Methods. Assumptions are resolved conservatively: an unquoted value falls back to the null (S5).

text: Specify the methods used to assess risk of bias in the included studies, including details of the tool(s) used, how many reviewers assessed each study and whether they worked independently, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process.
note: No risk-of-bias appraisal of included studies. The audit measures what studies report, not whether their estimates are correct; appraising them would be a different study.

text: Specify for each outcome the effect measure(s) (e.g. risk ratio, mean difference) used in the synthesis or presentation of results.
note: Completeness is a proportion; predictors are adjusted odds ratios from a mixed-effects logistic model at the study-determinant level.

text: Describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each synthesis.
note: Per-item denominators vary: conditional items are scored only where the triggering population is present.

text: Describe any methods required to prepare the data for presentation or synthesis, such as handling of missing summary statistics, or data conversions.
note: Composite quantities are computed in code from the item scores.

text: Describe any methods used to tabulate or visually display results of individual studies and syntheses.

Describe any methods used to synthesise results and provide a rationale for the choice(s). If meta-analysis was performed, describe the model(s), method(s) to identify the presence and extent of statistical heterogeneity, and software package(s) used.
note: No meta-analysis: effect estimates are not pooled. Predictors are modelled at the study-determinant level by mixed-effects logistic regression, with the rationale given; covariate-by-determinant heterogeneity is tested and reported.

text: Describe any methods used to explore possible causes of heterogeneity among study results.
note: Study-level predictors of completeness (calendar time, design, centre status, size, interventional design, outcome role, funding).

text: Describe any sensitivity analyses conducted to assess robustness of the synthesised results.
note: Eligibility definition, composition of the minimum set (leave-one-out and a de novo DSA substitution), author-group clustering, source format, retrieval representativeness.

text: Describe any methods used to assess risk of bias due to missing results in a synthesis (arising from reporting biases).
note: Addressed as selective reporting: whether completeness predicts reporting a significant exposure-to-CLAD effect. Exploratory.

text: Describe any methods used to assess certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence for an outcome.
note: No certainty rating. GRADE assesses confidence in an effect estimate; this review estimates no effect.

text: Describe the results of the search and selection process, from the number of records identified in the search to the number of studies included in the review, ideally using a flow diagram.
Cite studies that might appear to meet the inclusion criteria, but which were excluded, and explain why they were excluded.
note: Full-text exclusions are given as a single count with their reasons listed; per-reason counts are not broken out except for the studies excluded as not lung transplant recipients, which are recorded per identifier with a reason.

text: Cite each included study and present its characteristics.
note: Cohort characteristics by study design. Individual studies are not cited: {n_ana} studies are the unit of measurement, not of evidence.

text: Present assessments of risk of bias for each included study.
note: See item 11.

text: For all outcomes, present, for each study: (a) summary statistics for each group (where appropriate) and (b) an effect estimate and its precision, ideally using structured tables or plots.
note: No per-study effect estimates are extracted or presented; the outcome is measured on the study, not reported by it.

text: For each synthesis, briefly summarise the characteristics and risk of bias among contributing studies.
Present results of all statistical syntheses conducted.
Present results of all investigations of possible causes of heterogeneity among study results.
location: Results, Predictors of reporting completeness; Figure 3

text: Present results of all sensitivity analyses conducted to assess the robustness of the synthesised results.
Present assessments of risk of bias due to missing results (arising from reporting biases) for each synthesis assessed.
note: See item 14.

text: Present assessments of certainty (or confidence) in the body of evidence for each outcome assessed.
note: See item 15.

text: Provide a general interpretation of the results in the context of other evidence.
Discuss any limitations of the evidence included in the review.
Discuss any limitations of the review processes used.
note: Single-pass extraction; single expert coder, so no inter-rater ceiling; reporting is assessed from the published article.

text: Discuss implications of the results for practice, policy, and future research.
note: Proposes a minimum immunological reporting set.

text: Provide registration information for the review, including register name and registration number, or state that the review was not registered.
note: The review was not registered. PROSPERO registers reviews of health outcomes and does not cover a reporting-completeness audit.

text: Indicate where the review protocol can be accessed, or state that a protocol was not prepared.
note: No registered protocol. The instrument was locked before extraction: the covariate panel and its scoring anchors are reproduced in S6, and their pre-extraction version history is in the project repository.

text: Describe and explain any amendments to information provided at registration or in the protocol.
note: One amendment: an eligibility criterion excluding studies whose analysed population contains no lung transplant recipients was added after validation coding surfaced the omission; the records it excluded are listed by identifier. The minimum immunological set contains determinants of CLAD; the CLAD definition is an outcome-ascertainment item and is scored and reported as one, which is a scoping decision rather than an amendment.
